The County and SJCoC HHAP Round 6 local NOFA funds permanent housing operating costs and services, rental assistance and rapid rehousing, interim housing operations and services, and prevention and diversion; none is construction, and Labor Code 1720(a)(1) covers construction only. https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/578.99

set.prevailing_wage_basis: 24 CFR 983.153(c): for PBV development (new construction or rehabilitation under an Agreement) involving nine or more contract units, the owner and its contractors must pay Davis-Bacon wages; 42 U.S.C. 1437j(a) applies the same rule to nine or more Section 8 assisted units under an agreement made before construction. Does not apply to PBV on existing housing. https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/24/983.153

reason: Davis-Bacon applies to PBV development with nine or more contract units under 24 CFR 983.153(c).

set.prevailing_wage_basis: 42 U.S.C. 1437j(a) (Section 12 of the 1937 Act): contracts for public housing loans, contributions, sale or lease must require Davis-Bacon wages for laborers and mechanics in development of the project, including projects with nine or more Section 8 assisted units under an agreement made before construction; 24 CFR 983.153(c) applies Davis-Bacon to PBV development with nine or more contract units (RAD and Section 18 conversions to PBV). Labor Code 1720(c)(1) also removes the private residential exemption for projects built under an agreement with a local public housing authority. https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1437j

reason: Public housing and PBV development rules (42 U.S.C. 1437j(a), 24 CFR 983.153(c)) require Davis-Bacon wages.
